'''Peter Uetz''' (born 11 June 1965) is a German biologist. His research focuses on [[microbial systems biology]], [[molecular biology]], and [[herpetology]].

==Biography==
=== Early life and education ===
Uetz attended elementary school in Untergruppenbach and the [[Robert-Mayer-Gymnasium Heilbronn]], completing his ''Abitur'' in 1985. In 1982, he published his first popular-science report on the reproductive biology of [[chameleons]] as part of the Baden-Württemberg state competition of [[Jugend forscht]]. In 1987, together with [[Gunther Köhler]], he co-founded the Working Group on [[Iguanidae|iguanas]] within the [[German Society for Herpetology and Herpetoculture]] (DGHT) and launched the journal ''Iguana''.

From 1985 to 1986, he studied biology at the [[University of Stuttgart]], where he earned his preliminary diploma. In 1986, he developed a computer program for [[molecular genetics]], which won fifth place in the national ''Jugend forscht'' competition in biology.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.jugend-forscht.de/projektdatenbank/ein-comuterprogramm-zur-molekulargenetik.html |title=Jugend forscht: ''Ein Computerprogramm zur Molekulargenetik'' |access-date=2025-10-20 |archive-date=2018-10-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181029232427/https://www.jugend-forscht.de/projektdatenbank/ein-comuterprogramm-zur-molekulargenetik.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> 

From 1987 to 1988, he completed his civilian service at the Institute for Immunology at the [[University of Heidelberg]]. He continued his studies at the [[University of Tübingen]] in 1989 and later at Heidelberg, where he graduated in 1993 with a diploma thesis on the ''5-HT3'' receptor gene of mice, conducted at the [[Max Planck Institute for Medical Research]] in Heidelberg.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Uetz |first1=Peter |last2=Abdelatty |first2=Fawzy |last3=Villarroel |first3=Alfredo |last4=Rappold |first4=Gudrun |last5=Weiss |first5=Birgit |title=Organization of the murine 5-HT3 receptor gene and assignment to human chromosome 11 |journal=FEBS Letters |volume=339 |issue=3 |pages=302–306 |date=21 February 1994 |doi=10.1016/0014-5793(94)80435-4 |pmid=8112471 |bibcode=1994FEBSL.339..302U }}</ref>

In 1997, he earned his Ph.D. (''Dr. rer. nat.'') in developmental biology at the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] (EMBL), [[University of Heidelberg]], with a dissertation titled ''Biochemical Studies on the Limb Deformity Protein of Vertebrates''. His doctoral work produced two publications on protein–protein interactions and molecular biology.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Uetz |first1=P. |last2=Fumagalli |first2=S. |last3=James |first3=D. |last4=Zeller |first4=R. |title=Molecular interaction between limb deformity proteins (formins) and Src family kinases |journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry |volume=271 |issue=52 |pages=33525–33530 |date=27 December 1996 |doi=10.1074/jbc.271.52.33525 |doi-access=free |pmid=8969217}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Uetz |first1=P. |last2=Zeller |first2=R. |title=Vectors for expression of protein-A-tagged proteins in vertebrate cells |journal=Analytical Biochemistry |volume=237 |issue=1 |pages=161–163 |date=15 May 1996 |doi=10.1006/abio.1996.0220 |pmid=8660557}}</ref>

=== Career ===
In November 1995, Uetz co-founded the [[The Reptile Database|EMBL Reptile Database]] with Thure Etzold, a comprehensive online database of reptile taxonomy. As of December 2022, it included data on more than 11,900 species. His collaborators include [[Jakob Hallermann]], [[Jiří Hošek]], and a 34-member advisory board with scientists such as [[Aaron M. Bauer]], [[Frank Glaw]], [[Larry Lee Grismer]], [[Miguel Vences]], [[Sebastian Lotzkat]], and [[Thomas Ziegler (zoologist)|Thomas Ziegler]].

Following a postdoctoral fellowship at the [[University of Washington]] in [[Seattle]], Uetz became an associate professor at the [[J. Craig Venter Institute]] (JCVI) in [[Rockville, Maryland]] in 2006. In June 2007, he completed his habilitation at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] (then University of Karlsruhe). Since October 2011, he has been an [[associate professor]] at the Center for the Study of Biological Complexity, [[Virginia Commonwealth University]] (VCU), in [[Richmond, Virginia]].<ref name=bio/>

His research areas include microbial [[interactomics]], the interactomes of [[viruses]] and [[bacteriophages]], [[bioinformatics]] of protein networks, [[protein–protein interactions]], [[protein complexes]], [[protein domains]], and the [[biodiversity]] of [[reptiles]].<ref name=bio>Fabrizio Li Vigni (2013). ''A Life for Reptiles and Amphibians.'' Edition Chimaira. ISBN 978-3-89973-199-6. (Interview with Peter Uetz, pp. 141–145)</ref>

=== Science communication ===
Uetz has engaged in public discussions on [[evolution]] and [[creationism]], including a 2026 article published in ''[[Free Inquiry]]'' addressing claims made by chemist [[James Tour]].<ref name="Uetz-2026">{{Cite journal |last=Uetz |first=Peter |date=2026-07-23 |title=How a Respected Scientist Became a Creationist Superstar—and How To Debunk a Creationist 'Superstar'. |url=http://uetz.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Uetz_on_Tour.pdf |journal=[[Free Inquiry]] |volume=2026 |issue=August/September |pages=41–45}}</ref>

== Eponyms ==
Two reptile species have been named in his honor:
* The chameleon ''[[Calumma uetzi]]'' from [[Madagascar]] (2018).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Prötzel |first1=David |last2=Vences |first2=Miguel |last3=Hawlitschek |first3=Oliver |last4=Scherz |first4=Mark D. |last5=Ratsoavina |first5=Fanomezana M. |title=Endangered beauties: micro-CT cranial osteology, molecular genetics and external morphology reveal three new species of chameleons in the ''Calumma boettgeri'' complex (Squamata: Chamaeleonidae) |journal=Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=184 |issue=2 |pages=471–498 |date=5 October 2018 |doi=10.1093/zoolinnean/zlx112}}</ref>  
* The pit viper ''[[Trimeresurus uetzi]]'' from [[Myanmar]] (2023).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Vogel |first1=Gernot |last2=Nguyen |first2=Tan Van |last3=David |first3=Patrick |title=A new green pitviper of the ''Trimeresurus albolabris'' complex (Reptilia, Serpentes, Viperidae) from central and southern Myanmar |journal=Zootaxa |volume=5357 |issue=4 |pages=515–554 |date=20 October 2023 |doi=10.11646/zootaxa.5357.4.3 |pmid=38220633 }}</ref>
